text:
Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
[Repository README](../README.md) · [Development setup](setup.md) · [Validation](validation.md) · [Foundation versioning](versioning.md) · [ADR-0014](adr/0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) · [ADR-0017](adr/0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md)
This is the practical reference for turning a revision of Orion into a new, independent project and for keeping that project's foundation current: what to decide and provide, how to run the initialization, what the new repository contains, what to do next, and how provenance and foundation upgrades work. [ADR-0014](adr/0014-derive-projects-from-orion-through-git-ancestry-with-recorded-provenance.md) records the ancestry and provenance decision; [ADR-0017](adr/0017-start-derived-projects-from-a-clean-foundation-baseline.md) records the clean-baseline contract. The commands exist in every Orion checkout; the canonical Orion repository itself is never initialized as a project.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Model
text:
Model
The canonical `GabriellMDias/Orion` repository is the upstream development foundation. A derived project is an independent Git repository with its own `origin`, branches, pull requests, CI history, human actions, product decisions, and releases. It starts from a clean clone of Orion and keeps Orion's commit history, so Git can compute what changed upstream and merge it later, but its first commit removes Orion's own reference implementation and development history and gives the repository the project's identity.
Concern
Mechanism
Identity and provenance
[`.orion/project.json`](../.orion/project.json), validated by `pnpm orion:check`
Clean-baseline contract
[`.orion/derivation.json`](../.orion/derivation.json): foundation-only paths, project-owned files and their templates, and the foundation workspace package scope
Immutable starting point
`foundation.initializedFromCommit`: the published Orion commit the project was initialized from; never changes
Current foundation
`foundation.baselineCommit`: the newest Orion commit integrated and validated through a reviewed merge
Canonical upstream
Local remote `orion-upstream`: fetch-only (its push URL is disabled), fetches no tags, and is tracked by no local branch
Product repository
Recorded as `repository.url`; each clone's `origin` is that repository or a fork or mirror of it, never the foundation ([remote rules](#remote-rules))
In the Orion repository the manifest has `"kind": "foundation"` and only describes Orion. A derived project's manifest (schema version 2) has `"kind": "project"` and additionally records its npm `packageScope` and its foundation ancestry. The Living Documentation Portal links source files to the manifest's repository.
A derived project inherits [Apache-2.0-licensed Orion source](../LICENSE). The project remains responsible for licensing its independently created product code and for applicable obligations of inherited and third-party material; Orion's license does not choose the project's overall license.

heading: Next steps after creation
text:
Next steps after creation
The project's [README](../README.md) routes to its plan and human actions, which track these steps with stable IDs.
**Publish and validate (PH-01, PJ-01).** Push `main` to the new repository and confirm that `pnpm validate` passes locally and that the repository's CI runs.
**Protect the repository (PH-02 to PH-04).** Require pull requests and the `Orion required gate` check on `main`, keep merge commits available for foundation upgrades, enable Renovate, and enable the applicable GitHub security controls. Settings verified for Orion do not apply to the new repository.
**Onboard contributors.** Each clone needs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the local configuration from [setup](setup.md). Run `pnpm orion:upstream` and `git fetch orion-upstream` in any clone that will inspect or perform foundation upgrades; clones receive no `orion-upstream` remote automatically.
**Define the product (PH-05, PJ-02).** Record the product scope, actors, first capabilities, data classification, and acceptance criteria, then replace the README introduction and current state.
**Build the first module (PJ-03).** Add its schema, reviewed migration, contract, SDK use, web workflow, tests, and documentation as described for [API modules](../apps/api/README.md#modules) and [web modules](../apps/web/README.md#modules), and compose it in `apps/api/src/modules.ts` and `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`. [Orion's reference implementation](#orions-reference-implementation) shows a complete module.
**Replace the placeholder identity (PJ-04).** Replace the brand mark and regenerate the touch icon as described under [web identity](../apps/web/README.md#identity).
**Decide the product license (PH-06)** before distribution requires it.
**Add conditional work when it becomes real (PJ-05).** An identity provider, durable releases, or a deployment environment become new tasks and human actions in the project's own files.
Keep the project's plan and human actions current as work proceeds; `AGENTS.md` routes contributors and agents to them through the README's Current state.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Orion's reference implementation
text:
Orion's reference implementation
The Orion repository composes a complete Approval Request module that demonstrates the architecture from database to browser and is exercised by Orion's validation gate. It is foundation-only: initialization removes it, and no project-owned or shared file refers to it. To study it while building a module, read it in Orion at the commit recorded as the project's baseline, for example in a separate Orion clone or with `git show <baseline>:<path>` after `git fetch orion-upstream`. The paths it occupies are listed in [`.orion/derivation.json`](../.orion/derivation.json). Copy patterns, not the feature: a product module belongs under its own name and is composed in the project's `modules.ts` and `modules.tsx`.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Provenance and foundation upgrades
text:
Provenance and foundation upgrades
Provenance is what makes upgrades possible. Initialization records the Orion commit in both `foundation.initializedFromCommit`, which never changes, and `foundation.baselineCommit`. Because the project keeps Orion's history, Git can compute what changed upstream since the baseline and merge it with a normal three-way merge. Each upgrade merges a newer Orion commit with its history and then records it as the new baseline; `pnpm orion:check` verifies that the baseline is an ancestor of `HEAD`, and `pnpm orion:status` compares it with a fetched `orion-upstream`. The derivation contract travels with every upgrade, and `pnpm orion:prune` reapplies it, so the project stays free of foundation-only content and keeps its own package scope. [Stable semantic tags](versioning.md) make released foundation points easier to identify: a project may be described as derived from a tagged Orion release when its initialization commit matches that tag, while the manifest continues to record the exact commit SHA.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Inspect provenance
text:
Inspect provenance
pnpm orion:status

It prints the project identity and package scope, the initialization and recorded baseline commits, whether `orion-upstream` is configured and fetch-only, and, after `git fetch orion-upstream`, how many upstream commits follow the baseline and whether integrated commits are not yet recorded. It does not fetch or change anything.
`pnpm orion:check` runs in `pnpm validate`.
In Orion, it validates the manifest and derivation contract, requires every foundation-only path and template to exist, and rejects shared tracked files that link to, import, name, or mention foundation-only content. Derivation tooling, ADRs, this guide, and generated output are exempt.
In a project, it validates the manifest and contract, requires the project plan and human actions and the root package name of the recorded scope, rejects any foundation-only path and any remaining reference to the foundation package scope in code or configuration, requires both recorded commits to exist with the initialization commit an ancestor of the baseline and the baseline an ancestor of `HEAD`, and applies the [remote rules](#remote-rules). It needs full history; CI already uses `fetch-depth: 0`.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Remote rules
text:
Remote rules
Git remotes are local configuration, so other clones of the project do not receive `orion-upstream`. Configure it in any clone with:
pnpm orion:upstream
git fetch orion-upstream

Remote
Rule
Enforced by
`origin`
Must not identify the Orion foundation through its fetch or push URL, so product work never has the foundation as its normal push target. It need not equal the project's `repository.url`: contributors may work through a fork or mirror.
`pnpm orion:upstream` refuses; `pnpm orion:check` fails
`orion-upstream`, when present
Its fetch URL must identify the foundation repository recorded in the manifest.
`pnpm orion:upstream` refuses; `pnpm orion:check` fails
`orion-upstream`, when present
Its only push URL must be the disabled `orion-upstream-is-fetch-only`.
`pnpm orion:check` fails and directs you to rerun `pnpm orion:upstream`
`orion-upstream`, when absent
Valid; a normal clone has no foundation remote until a developer configures it.
—
Local branches
No local branch may track `orion-upstream`; an argument-free `git pull` would otherwise merge foundation changes outside a reviewed upgrade.
`pnpm orion:check` fails and directs you to rerun `pnpm orion:upstream`
`pnpm orion:upstream` adds `orion-upstream` from the manifest when absent, replaces every push URL of it with the disabled one, disables its tags, and removes upstream tracking of it from every local branch. It is safe to rerun.
Repository identities compare as normalized HTTPS URLs, so HTTPS, SSH, and scp-like forms of the same repository match. Host names are case-insensitive, but repository path case is significant because self-hosted servers may treat `acme/Ledger` and `acme/ledger` as different repositories: accepting a URL as a given repository, as for `orion-upstream` or the `origin` checked before initialization, requires the exact path. Refusing a URL because it could reach the foundation, as for `origin` or a new project's repository, ignores path case, because hosts such as GitHub resolve differently cased paths to the same repository. An explicit non-default HTTPS port is part of the identity: `https://git.example.com:8443/acme/ledger` differs from `https://git.example.com/acme/ledger`, while `:443` is the same endpoint as no port. A non-default SSH port only selects the SSH transport and does not identify the HTTPS endpoint, so such a URL is refused as a project repository and never matches the foundation; supply the repository's HTTPS URL instead.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Upgrade to a newer Orion revision
text:
Upgrade to a newer Orion revision
An upgrade is a normal reviewable engineering change on a branch. Nothing is applied automatically, and semantic conflicts are resolved by people or agents under review. Tags help humans choose a known release point but do not change this workflow. Ordinary conflicts in project-modified shared files do not by themselves indicate a MAJOR Orion release.
Run `git fetch orion-upstream` and `pnpm orion:status`. Review upstream changes with `git log --oneline <baseline>..orion-upstream/main` and `git diff <baseline> orion-upstream/main`, including ADRs, policies, migrations, tooling, and `.orion/derivation.json`.
Choose the candidate commit; it must be on `orion-upstream/main`. Create a branch, for example `git switch -c orion-upgrade/<short-commit>`, and run `git merge --no-ff <commit>`.
Resolve conflicts in `.orion/project.json`, `.orion/derivation.json`, the release registry, and `package.json` first if they prevent the command from loading. Run `pnpm orion:prune` while other merge conflicts remain. It deletes foundation-only paths the merge changed or added (resolving their modify/delete conflicts), renames foundation package-scope references in resolved shared files, and stages those changes. It leaves unresolved shared files and project-owned files untouched, reports the unresolved paths, and refuses to delete a recorded durable migration or follow linked paths outside the checkout. Resolve and stage reported conflicts, then rerun it.
Resolve remaining conflicts according to [content ownership](#content-ownership): keep the project's version of project-owned files and merge shared files. Never hand-merge generated output: run the generators from step 5, then stage their results (for example `git add -A apps/web/src/generated docs/generated packages/sdk/src/generated`), which resolves conflicts in generated files, including ones the project's output no longer contains. Rerun `pnpm orion:prune` until it reports no unresolved files. Review semantic interactions with product code even where Git reports no conflict.
Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm db:generate`, `pnpm -C apps/api references:write`, `pnpm -C packages/sdk generate`, `pnpm docs:references:write`, and `pnpm validate`. Commit the merge.
Run `pnpm orion:record-baseline <commit>`. It refuses unless the worktree is clean and `orion-upstream` exists and satisfies the [remote rules](#remote-rules). It then fetches `main` from that verified foundation, so refs fetched earlier from another repository cannot vouch for the commit. Finally it requires the commit to be on `orion-upstream/main`, descend from the recorded baseline, and already be an ancestor of `HEAD`. Commit the manifest change, rerun `pnpm validate`, and open the pull request against the project's `main`.
Merge the pull request with a merge commit. Squash or rebase merges discard Orion's commit identities, and `pnpm orion:check` then fails because the recorded baseline is not an ancestor of `HEAD`. The project repository must therefore keep merge commits enabled (project human action PH-02). This applies only to Orion upgrade pull requests.
If the project's default branch requires pull requests, as PH-02 establishes, the merge and baseline update reach `main` together through that pull request. Record the upgrade and any project-specific follow-up in the project plan.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Migrate a project from schema version 1
text:
Migrate a project from schema version 1
Projects initialized before the clean-baseline contract have a schema version 1 manifest with `referenceImplementations`, Orion's plan, human actions, and acceptance report, and usually the Approval Request implementation and `@orion/*` packages. After merging an Orion revision that contains this contract, `pnpm orion:check` refuses the old manifest. Migrate in the upgrade branch:
If the project adopted Approval Request as product behavior, move its code, schema, metadata, grants, and tests out of the foundation-only paths first (for example to `src/features/<product-module>/` and matching paths under the module's own name). Preserve every released migration at its original path and remove that path from the project's `foundationOnly` list in `.orion/derivation.json`; never rename or delete it. Verify uncertain release status under [migration policy](database/migrations.md) before classifying a migration as removable. Only genuinely unreleased reference migrations may be removed or renamed. `orion:prune` refuses removal of recorded durable migrations.
Edit `.orion/project.json`: set `schemaVersion` to `2`, remove `referenceImplementations`, and add `"packageScope": "@<scope>"`.
Run `pnpm orion:prune` to remove foundation-only paths and rename package-scope references.
Replace the project-owned files that still carry Orion's content: render `README.md`, `apps/api/src/modules.ts`, `apps/web/src/modules.tsx`, and the brand assets from the [templates](../.orion/derivation.json) (substituting each `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`), keeping existing project-specific text. Keep `docs/project/`; remove its references to Orion's plan, human actions, acceptance report, and reference implementation, and port the maintenance rules from the plan and human-action templates.
Regenerate as in [upgrade step 5](#upgrade-to-a-newer-orion-revision), run `pnpm validate`, and continue with baseline recording.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Contributing improvements back to Orion
text:
Contributing improvements back to Orion
Product work never goes to `orion-upstream`; its push URL is disabled. To improve the foundation itself, make the change in a separate clone of Orion and submit it there under Orion's own review, then adopt it in projects through the upgrade workflow. Do not move product code, requirements, or history into Orion. In Orion, keep new shared content independent of foundation-only content; extend `.orion/derivation.json` when adding foundation-only or project-owned files.

title: Start and Upgrade a Project from Orion
heading: Limits
text:
Limits
Provenance proves which Orion commits are ancestors of the project; it does not prove that the project still follows every inherited policy. Validation and review remain the enforcement.
`pnpm orion:check` can verify that the recorded baseline is integrated, but only `pnpm orion:status` with a fetched upstream can report newer integrated commits that were not yet recorded.
Upgrades that change foundation-only or project-owned files conflict in projects; projects that diverge heavily from shared files should expect more conflicts there.
The isolation check matches links, imports, path names, and listed terms; it cannot judge whether shared prose implicitly assumes the reference implementation. Review remains necessary.
The immutable Git commit remains the exact foundation revision and provenance identity. [Foundation versioning](versioning.md) assigns human-readable tags only to deliberate stable release points; commits between tags remain usable by SHA.

heading: Owner-authorized revision
text:
Owner-authorized revision
The subsequent implementation request authorized all phases and delegated technical decisions without phase-by-phase approval. The owner also explicitly approved necessary real business data in OpenAI requests and reuse of the existing API key for synthetic evaluations. The former opaque-only/privacy-decision gate below is historical and does not block ordinary in-scope analysis. title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Recommendation
text:
Recommendation
Evolve IA-MNS into a conversational assistant that can reason over authorized context, write its own responses, and choose among controlled business tools. Keep data access, authorization, business definitions, query compilation, arithmetic, and execution limits in the application. The model should decide how to help within those boundaries, including when no new database query is necessary.
This addresses a broad class of requests: summarize, explain, rewrite, translate, compare available facts, adjust presentation, continue an analysis, and combine supported operations. Each phrasing should not require a new intent, conditional branch, prompt exception, or business capability. New data sources, metrics, business meanings, and side effects still require explicit integration and validation.
The immediate recommendation is a general conversation and evidence layer over the existing capabilities, followed by a bounded tool-calling loop. Retain the existing Responses API integration, PostgreSQL history, semantic product catalogs, and reviewed ERP adapters. Do not start by replacing the stack, adding multiple agents, fine-tuning, or exposing a SQL console.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: What the repository shows
text:
What the repository shows
This analysis inspected the actual working tree, including substantial pre-existing uncommitted sales/product work, on top of `885cf58`. That commit alone does not identify everything analyzed. The reported conversation was not replayed against the live model; no stored private conversation, ERP data, credentials, or operational model setting was read. The diagnosis below is supported by executable code and current policy, not a claim about the exact model output in that turn.
Finding
Evidence
Effect
The router can choose a registered capability or a small social/unavailable intent. It is expressly forbidden to produce answers or public prose.
[`routeSchema` and `createAgentPlanner`](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/planner.ts)

Business answers in router history are replaced by an answer-delivered marker.
[`runAgentTurn`](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/application.ts)
The model cannot read the figures or explanation behind “summarize this.”
Sales interpretation sees filters, active/pending plans, and filter-only descriptions of answers. It cannot emit figures or public text.
[`interpreterState`, `interpreterInstructions`, `interpreterMessages`](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/interpreter.ts); [`recordExchange` use](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/application.ts)
Sales context supports query refinement, not discussion of the returned evidence.
The exact reported refusal is a fixed sales message.
`unsupportedMessage` in [`sales/application.ts`](../../apps/api/src/features/sales/application.ts)
The reported wording is consistent with the sales unsupported branch. The route/interpretation for the specific incident remains unverified.
Each model request forces exactly one named strict function call, then consumes only its validated arguments.
[`StructuredModel`](../../apps/api/src/ai/model.ts), [`createOpenAiModel`](../../apps/api/src/ai/openai.ts)
There is no general response-generation or iterative tool-result conversation in this adapter.

[`AgentRepository`](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/prisma-repository.ts), [`storedReplySchema`](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/contracts.ts)
The information is not necessarily lost. The missing piece is authorized, purpose-specific model context. Older references need bounded retrieval beyond that window.
Product choices and sales scope already have structured, ERP-specific state and complete-membership execution.
[`products/sales.ts`](../../apps/api/src/features/products/sales.ts), [semantic sales integration](../architecture/semantic-product-resolution.md#sales-integration)
Preserve and reuse this work; do not reconstruct a product selection from a displayed list or prose.
The chat sends text and a source selection and renders structured results with a text message.
[`agent/contracts.ts`](../../apps/api/src/features/agent/contracts.ts), [`agent/page.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/features/agent/page.tsx), [`ModelMessage`](../../apps/api/src/ai/model.ts)
File/image ingestion and evidence-aware prose need actual contracts and UI support; choosing a multimodal model alone does not implement them.
The source inspection explains the failure class: IA-MNS currently uses the model as an interpreter for a restricted query workflow. It does not expose the broader conversational abilities needed to discuss an answer. Changing only the model or adding a synonym for “resumo” would leave these architectural restrictions in place.
These restrictions were deliberate. [ADR-0018](../adr/0018-bound-natural-language-sales-to-a-read-only-query-capability.md), [ADR-0019](../adr/0019-compose-a-corporate-agent-with-durable-conversations.md), and [ADR-0024](../adr/0024-interpret-analytics-through-structured-state-and-evaluate-ai-behavior.md) retain application-authored responses, deterministic financial results, and figure-free model context. A future implementation must explicitly extend or partially supersede the affected decisions rather than silently contradict them.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: What “use ChatGPT's capabilities” means here
text:
What “use ChatGPT's capabilities” means here
The requested behavior is feasible using the API: a model can receive conversation context, call application functions, and produce an answer after seeing the tool results. Responses also supports file and image inputs, subject to model and input-type support. IA-MNS must implement the surrounding context, tools, permissions, persistence, and presentation; an API model setting does not import the ChatGPT application's complete product behavior. See the official [conversation-state](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state), [function-calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling), [file-input](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs), and [vision](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision) documentation.
The goal is broad conversational competence over controlled resources. The agent may explain concepts from general knowledge, clearly distinguish that from company facts, and transform user-provided material. Claims about MNS or its operations require authorized evidence. If the required evidence or tool is absent, it should describe the specific gap and any useful supported next step.
This reduces configuration of language and workflows. It cannot eliminate the need to define what “sales,” “net value,” “active product,” or a source-specific unit means. Neither a schema nor a powerful model can reliably infer all business rules, undocumented join cardinalities, or organizational permissions.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Proposed division of responsibility
text:
Proposed division of responsibility
Concern
Model autonomy
Server authority
Conversation
Understand intent, references, tone, language, desired format, and level of detail.
Select authorized history and protect conversation ownership.
Planning
Answer directly, inspect evidence, request a supported analysis, or ask a meaningful clarification.
Admit only registered tools, valid arguments, permitted scopes, and bounded work.
Product interpretation
Use reviewed semantic descriptions and actual candidates; reuse an explicit prior choice.
Validate catalog version, ERP, grounding, ambiguity, and complete selection membership.
Analysis
Choose useful supported comparisons and decompositions for the user's objective.
Enforce metric meaning, source selection, date limits, unit compatibility, and exact calculations.
Response
Write natural prose, explain supported findings, propose hypotheses, and adapt presentation.
Bind factual claims to evidence, render canonical values, and reject unsafe or unverifiable outputs.
Learning
Adapt within the conversation and propose reusable preferences or new semantic candidates.
Control persistence, scope, review, revocation, and promotion into business knowledge.
External actions
Explain or prepare a proposed action when supported.
No ERP writes or outbound delivery tools in the initial design. Future side effects need their own authorization and delivery contract.
Autonomy applies to completing the current user request. It does not imply background monitoring, scheduled jobs, self-modification, permission changes, or unattended external writes.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Architecture
text:
Architecture
flowchart TD

    H[(IA-MNS history and evidence)] --> C

All components below are proposed responsibilities, not claims that new files, tool names, or APIs already exist.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: 1. Conversation with evidence
text:
1. Conversation with evidence
Extend the existing agent layer to assemble recent user/assistant messages, active and pending analysis state, the current focus, and references to relevant validated results. Persisted PostgreSQL records remain canonical; do not replace them with model memory or automatically send every historical result to the provider.
Represent a result as a versioned evidence object linked to its originating turn. Include source, absolute period, metric and unit, validated filters, semantic-selection provenance, catalog version, observation time, completeness/truncation status, warnings, and the permissions required to read it. Keep exact values as canonical decimal strings. Use the existing reply snapshot where possible; a separate table is justified only if lifecycle or querying needs it.
Before including any evidence, check current ownership and all dependent permissions. Repeat those checks when retrieving older turns, composing results, returning a stored response, or replaying a request. A summary derived from semantic sales inherits both `sales:read` and `products:read`; saving it as a generic conversation message with `capabilityId: null` must not bypass revocation. Derived prose, compacted memory, and exported artifacts inherit the union of their evidence dependencies.
Resolve “disso” to the current conversational focus, usually the most recent applicable result. Preserve explicitly selected product scope, source, period, and caveats. If several results are equally plausible, ask which one. If the referent is missing, deleted, inaccessible, or outside recoverable history, say so; do not reconstruct facts from general knowledge.
Use a token budget with recent messages plus targeted retrieval of older evidence. Optional compacted summaries are derived navigation aids, never the sole source of financial facts, permissions, or pending decisions. Keep evidence references and structured selections available after compaction, reload, and restart. Cross-chat retrieval and persistent user preferences should be separate explicit capabilities, not implicit global memory.
Manual context management with `store:false` is the recommended starting point because IA-MNS already owns its durable history and authorization. If an iterative Responses exchange is replayed manually, preserve the protocol items needed for continuation, including tool-call/output association and supported reasoning items; do not reduce a tool exchange to `output_text`. Provider-managed conversations or response chains would add retention/deletion obligations and are not required for this proposal. See [conversation state](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state).

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: 2. A model that can answer or use tools
text:
2. A model that can answer or use tools
Introduce a conversational model interface alongside the current structured interpretation port. It must support direct responses, multiple permitted tool definitions, tool results, and bounded continuation. Preserve strict argument schemas and application validation. The current router must not remain a mandatory gate that rejects a writing request before the conversational model sees it.
The server loop is: prepare authorized context; request a response or tool call; validate and execute an allowed call; project its evidence; continue until a final response, clarification, refusal, error, or budget limit. Tool outputs are data, not new instructions. The model proposes the sequence; code authorizes every step. This follows the [function-calling pattern](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling), with IA-MNS-specific limits.
Start with one orchestrator and the existing OpenAI SDK. An Agents SDK or other framework may reduce orchestration work later, but it is not a prerequisite. Framework choice must be evaluated against existing cancellation, tracing, persistence, and provider-data controls; it must not become a reason to enable extra tools or external traces.
Proposed tool responsibility
Existing foundation
Required boundary
Describe available business analyses and reviewed metric meanings.
Capability registry, sales catalog, product semantic catalogs.
Return permitted semantic descriptions, not raw schema, credentials, or unavailable capabilities.
Read relevant conversation evidence.
Owner-scoped turns and bounded reply snapshots.
Check ownership, dependencies, version, and field-level projection.
Resolve or refine a product selection.
Product resolver and source-specific AST.
Return validated candidates or a server-issued selection reference; preserve ambiguity and source isolation.
Execute a structured sales analysis.
Sales validation, period resolution, readers, fixed queries, decimal computation.
Revalidate every filter and selection; retain reference grain, date/result limits, and permissions.
Derive supported comparisons or prepare a table/chart from evidence.
Existing comparison and result machinery, extended only where needed.
Calculate in code; expose only implemented operations; validate units, compatible periods, and completeness.
Initially, adapters may reuse current capability execution. The target interface should accept validated structured plans or selection references rather than repeatedly reinterpreting a natural-language request at every layer. Reuse the domain validators/compiler; do not create a second sales semantics engine. Existing strict interpreters remain useful wherever a bounded interpretation step adds reliability.
The model must not broaden a request after a tool rejects a filter, loses a permission, encounters a stale selection, or reaches a size limit. It may repair a schema error once within budget if user intent is unchanged; it may not silently remove conditions to obtain an answer. A mixed request requiring unsupported business data must remain explicit about that limitation. Rewriting an existing answer, however, should not be classified as a new unsupported sales metric.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: 3. Natural language grounded in verified facts
text:
3. Natural language grounded in verified facts
Send only the evidence needed to answer. For a narrative summary, this might be the selected product scope, period, per-source totals, units, and relevant caveats. A request for a monthly trend requires actual monthly evidence; a single total does not support a claim of growth. Additional metrics, comparisons, and ratios must come from a validated computation, not model arithmetic.
Use evidence-linked response segments for quantitative statements: a segment references a known fact or deterministic derived fact with its measure, source, period, unit, and polarity. The renderer inserts the canonical value. For example, a synthetic paragraph template can refer to `sales.total` and `sales.period` without allowing the model to invent a financial amount. The model still chooses the surrounding explanation, ordering, and style.
Validate the relationship, not merely whether a number appears somewhere in a result. The same amount can be attributed to the wrong ERP or period. Mandatory caveats, incomplete-source status, and current-registration semantics must survive rewriting. Avoid merging `Tudo` results: the current source policy presents them separately. Zero, no data, unavailable data, and an undefined percentage are different states.
Structured output and numeric binding do not prove that every sentence is true. A model can use valid facts with misleading causality, comparisons, or certainty. Keep a clear distinction between observations and hypotheses; do not state a cause, forecast, or recommendation as an established company fact without evidence. Use semantic evaluations and review, with conservative rendering for financial assertions. If a response cannot pass its evidence checks, retain the validated result and offer a safe explanation or fallback rather than publishing unsupported prose.
The UI should retain structured result cards and provenance while permitting prose-only follow-ups. Tables and charts should use approved renderers and server-issued data references. Do not render model HTML, JavaScript, remote image URLs, or executable chart specifications. Text generation does not require replacing the current visual language or introducing streaming; if streaming is later added, financial assertions need validation before display.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: 4. Semantic knowledge that does not require rules for every phrase
text:
4. Semantic knowledge that does not require rules for every phrase
Maintain the distinction between business knowledge and language interpretation. Continue to describe each data source through reviewed entities, relationships, measures, dimensions, units, defaults, and examples. Let the model combine those concepts and choose workflows. Retrieve relevant catalog descriptions rather than stuffing the entire schema into every prompt.
The existing product catalogs, targeted metadata retrieval, and complete-selection compiler are a strong foundation. Discovery may propose new relationships or meanings; runtime should use only reviewed, executable entries. Granting access to a column does not verify its semantics or activate it. Current open dimensions and business questions remain governed by [PJ-36](implementation-plan.md#current-work), [PH-28](human-actions.md#ph-28), and the domain documentation.
Keep a confirmed “apple” selection within the conversation. A later summary or period change should not reopen the same ambiguity. For a new ambiguous request, weigh whether the choice materially changes the result: formatting and harmless presentation choices can be automatic; fruit versus every description containing the word can change financial totals and may warrant clarification. Model confidence alone is insufficient evidence to silently select the business scope.
Optional durable preferences can reduce repeated questions across chats, but they must be explicit, user-scoped, ERP/catalog-version-scoped, inspectable, correctable, and revocable. One person's choice must not silently redefine “apple” for the entire company. Suggested synonyms and business definitions enter a review queue; they do not modify code, prompts, permissions, or the catalog autonomously.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: 5. Files and images as another evidence source
text:
5. Files and images as another evidence source
File and image understanding is a later, separable capability. It is not needed to fix discussion of results already held by IA-MNS. Implement uploads, ownership, type/size/page limits, malware and parser isolation where applicable, protected storage, lifecycle/deletion, and model-safe content projection. Do not accept arbitrary file paths or fetch model-selected URLs.
For a document, retain page/section provenance; for an image, preserve its reference and indicate uncertainty in extracted text. Treat embedded instructions as untrusted document content. A file's claim about a sales amount is user-supplied evidence, not automatically an ERP-reconciled fact. Spreadsheet totals need complete, validated parsing and deterministic calculation; partial extraction cannot establish full-workbook totals. Supported file processing varies by type, as described in the official [file-input guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs), while image analysis needs a [vision-capable integration](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision).
For large document collections, add permission-aware retrieval only when needed. Revalidate authorization before returning a passage; bind citations to the correct file version and propagate deletion to extracted text, indexes, caches, and provider objects. Vector retrieval is an optional search technique, not a replacement for business queries or an immediate requirement for this conversation problem.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Privacy decision required before real-result narration
text:
Privacy decision required before real-result narration
Today, sales results and financial response prose are deliberately kept out of OpenAI requests. Reusing the same provider or keeping `store:false` does not authorize expanding that payload. [Data classification](../security/data-classification.md) and [retention](../security/data-retention.md) apply to every projection and derived response.
Option
Model receives
Tradeoff
Minimized business evidence — recommended, subject to approval.
Only authorized aggregates, labels, period, source, warnings, and selected deterministic derived facts needed for the task.
Enables richer analysis and explanation; expands the external processing of confidential business data.
Opaque fact references with local value substitution.
Approved labels/structure and fact identifiers; financial values stay on the server.
Supports flexible rewriting and presentation with less disclosure; the model cannot freely reason about hidden magnitudes. Even qualitative comparisons can disclose information and need classification.
The second option still changes the application-authored-prose rule, but can support an incremental design if sending financial values is not approved. Neither option entails sending raw ERP rows, customer records, connection settings, or entire conversations by default. The first better matches the requested analytical autonomy.
Before using real evidence, record the allowed fields, purposes, provider/account controls, retention/deletion, access, and applicable residency requirements. Resolve this through the existing [PH-09](human-actions.md#ph-09) policy work and, for production, [PH-23](human-actions.md#ph-23). A single reviewed data-processing policy should cover ordinary in-scope summaries; users should not face a fresh approval prompt for every paraphrase.
OpenAI distinguishes application state from abuse-monitoring retention. `store:false` alone is not Zero Data Retention; availability and restrictions of retention controls depend on account and feature configuration. Those settings were not verified in this analysis. See the official [data-controls documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data).

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Security and operating limits
text:
Security and operating limits
Risk
Proposed enforcement
Accessing another person's results or retaining revoked access through prose.
Scope history/evidence by verified owner; check current dependent permissions at context assembly, tool execution, publication, history access, and replay; cover derived messages and compacted state.
Instructions hidden in a product description, attachment, or tool result.
Keep fixed policy separate from untrusted content; use typed tool arguments and minimized outputs; enforce authority outside the model; test adversarial content.
Raw SQL, schema exploration, arbitrary network calls, or secret access.
Expose none of these as runtime tools. Retain reviewed compilers and isolated Administration/Discovery. A model never obtains ERP or provider credentials.
Financial errors or unsupported conclusions.
Deterministic calculations, evidence-bound quantitative claims, per-source results, explicit warnings, semantic evaluations, and safe fallback.
Accidental data transmission through prose, links, traces, or artifacts.
Authorize/minimize context before transmission; use safe text/renderers and allowlisted destinations; disable external tracing of content by default; inherit classification and retention for derivatives.
Infinite planning, repeated expensive queries, or budget exhaustion.
Server-enforced call/token/time/query budgets, repeated-call detection, cancellation propagation, and a clear terminal response. Model confidence or tool annotations do not override limits.
Replaying a turn after an unknown outcome.
Preserve existing request UUID and persistence semantics; do not restart chargeable work automatically or revive interrupted execution on reload.
Cross-source or stale semantic reuse.
Bind evidence and selections to ERP, catalog version, observation time, and permissions. Refuse invalid reuse without broadening to all products.
Prompt instructions are useful but are not an authorization boundary. Official [agent-safety guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder-safety) discusses untrusted inputs, data leakage, and structured isolation; it also recognizes residual risk. This proposal applies those principles without selecting Agent Builder or assuming perfect injection prevention.
Start with conservative experimental budgets: up to four model requests and six tool invocations per turn, an explicit total token allowance, and the existing 90-second turn deadline, whichever limit is reached first. These are candidate limits for measurement, not implemented settings or a promise that all semantic workflows fit. Retain tighter domain/query limits and reserve time for final composition. Measure latency and cost before revising them; do not simply extend every timeout.
Keep metadata traces for model/prompt/tool versions, permissions decisions, safe outcome codes, tool counts, tokens, latency, and evidence-validation failures. Do not log confidential prompts, results, attachments, model reasoning, or raw provider output. Any stored provider continuation items inherit confidential handling and need a defined lifecycle; operational traces should not become a second conversation archive.
The current [PH-30](human-actions.md#ph-30) record reports inherited VRMaster `PUBLIC` CREATE/TEMP privileges. This analysis did not re-audit the live database. Do not describe the database identity as effectively incapable of all DDL while that item is open. The proposed runtime tools remain fixed read operations; the documented ACL gap is a reason to retain that boundary, not to introduce arbitrary execution or change global grants within this work.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Expected behavior for the motivating case
text:
Expected behavior for the motivating case
The following dialogue uses the reported wording as a behavioral example, with no real sales values or product counts.
**“Quanto vendi de maçã nos últimos 3 meses?”** The assistant resolves the period using the existing business-date rule and requests a sales analysis. If the product resolver finds materially different meanings, it asks one focused choice.
**“Opção 1.”** The pending sales request resumes with the confirmed semantic selection. The server computes the answer and saves its evidence, explicit period, source, warnings, and selection provenance. Displayed product-list limits must not become limits on sales membership.
**“Me passe um resumo disso em forma de texto contínuo.”** The assistant uses that stored evidence, checks current permissions, and writes a paragraph. It does not execute another ERP query, change filters, ask for the period again, or route the request through the unsupported-sales branch.
**“Mais curto” / “Explique para alguém que não é da área” / “Traduza para inglês.”** The same conversation mechanism transforms the answer without new intent-specific implementation.
**“E em relação aos três meses anteriores?”** This requires a comparison. The assistant uses supported tools while preserving scope, and must distinguish three prior completed calendar months from the existing `previous_period` rule, which uses an equal number of days. It must use valid explicit ranges where supported or explain the limitation; it must not silently substitute one meaning for the other.
**“Por que caiu?”** If the evidence contains a decline, it can describe it and investigate available breakdowns. It cannot assert a cause from totals alone. It should label hypotheses and name any missing evidence, such as stock availability or pricing, without pretending those tools exist.
For “last three months,” keep the existing default of three completed calendar months. A prose-only follow-up preserves the originally executed dates even if the calendar has advanced. “Atualize com os dados de hoje” authorizes a fresh read within existing permissions; the answer should identify that it is new evidence.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Incremental implementation proposal
text:
Incremental implementation proposal
These phases are recommendations, not activated tasks. The existing implementation plan and human-action statuses are unchanged by this analysis.
Phase
Deliverable
Acceptance before proceeding
A. Agree on boundaries and characterize behavior.
A new reviewed ADR specifying which parts of ADR-0018/0019/0024 change; the allowed provider projection; synthetic baseline conversations and data-handling tests.
Privacy option selected; authorization/provenance design covers derived prose; existing numerical/domain guarantees retained. Real-data work remains gated by the applicable policy.
B. General conversational responses over existing evidence.
Authorized context builder, evidence references, free-form response composition with grounded facts, generic rewriting/explanation, compatible history/UI rendering, deterministic fallback.
The motivating dialogue and varied reformulations pass; summaries cause zero new ERP reads; no lost pending state or source scope; revocation blocks derived responses.
C. Bounded tool planning and composition.
One conversational orchestrator choosing among registered read/analysis tools; structured domain entry points; cancellation, budgets, provenance, and failure handling.
Unseen combinations of supported operations succeed without phrase-specific branches; all attempted tool calls are validated; unsupported scope never broadens silently.
D. Attachments and retrieval.
Authorized file/image ingestion, provenance, safe extraction, lifecycle, and optional retrieval over approved documents.
The assistant summarizes uploaded material with correct provenance; injection, cross-owner access, incomplete extraction, and deletion tests pass.
E. Deliberate preference memory and continuous improvement.
User-managed persistent preferences; reviewed semantic candidates; evaluation-driven prompt/model changes.
Preferences do not become global business rules, survive only their intended lifecycle, and cannot weaken permissions or query semantics.
Phase B is the smallest useful implementation that fixes the reported class of failures. Phase C is the broader autonomy direction. Files, vector search, and long-term memory should not block delivery of conversation over results already available.
Roll out behind a reversible server-side feature flag with the current behavior as fallback. Start with synthetic data, then a separately authorized local real-data pilot, then selected authenticated users after applicable operational prerequisites. Shadow comparisons must follow the same provider-data policy; sending real data in shadow mode is still transmission. Do not automatically rerun ERP reads to measure quality. Rollback must preserve readable history and its permission dependencies, not discard new replies or expose them as unprotected generic messages.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Validation and success criteria
text:
Validation and success criteria
Build on the existing [AI evaluation framework](../architecture/ai-evaluation.md), which already supports curated multi-turn cases, deterministic replay, live model comparison, and unreviewed synthetic candidates. Test families and invariants rather than maintaining one patch per wording. Compare the current pipeline and the proposed one on the same synthetic cases, with prompt/model/tool versions recorded.
Family
Required evidence
Narrative transformations
Summary, continuous prose, shorter/longer versions, explanation, translation, and drafting from results without a phrase whitelist. Exact facts and caveats preserved; no unnecessary ERP read.
Context continuity
Product choice, intervening social messages, multiple results, older referenced turns, restart, compaction, source changes, deleted/inaccessible evidence, and unresolved ambiguity.
Numerical truth
Decimal values, quantity units, unavailable VRMaster weight, zero/empty results, undefined percentages, mixed units, partial source failures, and truncated display lists.
Composed analysis
Valid comparisons and breakdowns, explicit period semantics, complete product membership, no invented dimensions, and no interpretation of a presentation request as a new query.
Authorization
Another owner's IDs, missing/revoked permissions, semantic sales dependencies, saved prose/history/replay, and future attachment/reference isolation.
Adversarial inputs
Instructions in messages, product labels, documents, and tool output; forged references; requests for SQL, credentials, writes, or external transmission; repeated-call and oversized-context attacks.
Operations
Cancellation, deadline and token/call limits, interrupted leases, provider refusal/incomplete output, safe fallback, no automatic chargeable retries, and accurate progress.
Attachments, when implemented
Provenance, extraction fidelity/completeness, damaged files, misleading images, upload authorization, safe rendering, and deletion of derivatives.
Deterministic checks must cover all access, arithmetic, provenance-reference, query-scope, and execution-budget invariants. Use human review and optionally an advisory model judge for clarity, relevance, and unsupported qualitative claims; a judge must not be the sole authority for financial or security correctness. Generated cases remain candidates until reviewed, as today.
Suggested release criteria: all deterministic safety/domain gates pass; zero unauthorized calls or unsupported numeric claims in the curated suite; at least 95% successful completion on a reviewed held-out set of supported conversations; zero ERP calls for pure rewriting of available evidence. Track unnecessary clarifications, false refusals, evidence fidelity, p50/p95 latency, tool counts, and cost per completed request. These are proposed targets, not measured results or proof of universal reliability. Establish acceptable latency and spend from the pilot before shared rollout.

title: Proposal: Conversational Autonomy with Controlled Business Tools
heading: Decisions to make at implementation time
text:
Decisions to make at implementation time

title: Corporate Agent Verification
heading: Scope and evidence boundary
text:
Scope and evidence boundary
Verification on 2026-10-01 covers PJ-09 in this local checkout. Existing uncommitted MVP work was preserved. The owner authorized reuse of the configured OpenAI key; no key was created or rotated. Oracle operations were read-only. PostgreSQL writes affect only IA-MNS's application history. No Git publication, remote CI, production identity or new business domain was performed.
The corporate agent has one registered business capability, sales. Social/capability replies use bounded routing and application-owned Portuguese prose. Business numbers retain the original controlled SQL, decimal aggregation and deterministic renderer. The reference excludes computed non-sale movements rather than subtracting returns; requests to include returns are explicitly unavailable. New identity/history work does not redefine that rule.

title: Corporate Agent Verification
heading: Changes and relevant guarantees
text:
Changes and relevant guarantees
A composed agent owns routing, implemented capability metadata, permissions, persistent conversation/context and real progress. Sales retains its domain executor; both legacy and agent transports share one Oracle pool.
PostgreSQL acceptance uses owner-scoped row locks, ordered turns, request UUID replay/conflict, atomic outcomes and a crash lease. Failed/interrupted turns preserve trusted filters and cannot invent answers. No provider call is automatically retried.
Result snapshots and context have stored versions. Sales context remains independent of intervening social turns; at most 12 sales questions/clarifications enter interpretation. Financial results never enter OpenAI requests.
Reading historical business answers enforces current capability permission as well as ownership. Runtime PostgreSQL credentials cannot create tables. Administrative migration credentials are removed from the API process before infrastructure imports.
The UI uses generated SDK operations, previous conversations, reload/continuation, explicit deletion and recovery of unknown acceptance with the original request UUID. Credentials/transcripts remain out of browser storage; only a light/dark preference is persisted there.
Progress is emitted before actual routing, sales interpretation, Oracle execution and deterministic result organization. Social, unsupported and clarification paths do not emit an Oracle stage.

title: Corporate Agent Verification
heading: Local infrastructure and runtime findings
text:
Local infrastructure and runtime findings
`pnpm db:local` provisioned PostgreSQL 16 at `127.0.0.1:55432`, applied the reviewed additive migration and restricted runtime grants, and updated only ignored local database settings. Existing OpenAI/Oracle settings were preserved. The named Docker volume retains application history. A Docker Desktop startup failure required moving its verified transient `run` directory to `run.recovery-20261001`; no Docker image/volume data was deleted.
A cold real Oracle query exceeded the previous 30-second native round-trip limit (`NJS-123`) and correctly persisted a failed turn without a result. The limit is now 45 seconds, within the agent's 90-second overall deadline. There is no automatic retry. Historical native-client compatibility and fetch limitations remain documented in [PH-08](human-actions.md#ph-08).

text:
Validation evidence
Frozen dependency installation and the complete local `pnpm validate` passed: format, lint, types, architectural boundaries, documentation/instructions, environment metadata, migration/provenance guards, generated API/database/SDK/portal checks, 92 API tests, 63 web unit tests, five browser component tests, builds/bundle checks, process smoke and all 20 end-to-end journeys. Remote CI was not run. An earlier complete run retained a historical failure in one shell journey that expected the removed documentation CTA; after updating it to exercise the real application navigation, its focused rerun and the complete gate passed. Final documentation/artifact consistency checks were repeated after recording these results.
The tests use synthetic providers and migrated PostgreSQL to cover ownership/current permission, concurrent acceptance, replay/conflict, lease interruption, paging, cascade deletion, context continuity, malformed provider output, redaction, truthful progress, history/reload, unknown acceptance, token memory, light/dark desktop/mobile and accessibility. Synthetic screenshots contain no ERP data. Both themes and the mobile layout were visually inspected.
Fourteen real HTTP scenarios passed using the existing key, actual routing/planning and Oracle 12.1.0.2 in Thick mode. Eight numerical answers were independently reconciled against the owner's complete original reference projection, including grouped rows, unit-specific totals, product sets, prior-year rows and percentage changes. Reference operations ran in a separate READ ONLY snapshot; no financial values or credentials are copied into this report.

text:
Sidebar organization and local upgrade (2026-10-02)
PJ-13 adds an animated, resizable desktop sidebar with a 60-pixel collapsed icon rail. New conversation, title/question search, pinned/archived views, documentation and theme selection live in the sidebar; each history row has a native menu for rename, pin/unpin, archive/restore and delete. Pointer and keyboard resizing, reduced motion, mobile modal focus and row-specific actions are covered by browser journeys. Original shared light/dark palettes and sales semantics are unchanged.
The additive `202610020001_conversation_organization` migration was applied to the existing local PostgreSQL database without resetting it. Real local HTTP calls verified title/favorite/archive updates, case-insensitive owned search, restoration and deletion. A fresh database connection read the saved metadata; after removing only the synthetic verification conversation, the existing history count matched. No OpenAI or Oracle request was needed. Migrated disposable-PostgreSQL tests additionally cover manual-title preservation, busy/owner validation, archive/replay/context continuation, literal wildcard escaping and favorite-first pagination.
The complete local `pnpm validate` passed after corrections: 95 API tests, 63 web unit tests, five browser component tests and 23 end-to-end journeys, including desktop/mobile accessibility and documentation navigation. The first full run exposed default-scope URL pollution and an accessibility test racing initial rendering; the default active view now keeps the canonical home URL clean, and the test awaits the visible workspace before analysis. No check was disabled or weakened. Generated API/SDK/schema/portal references were refreshed from their sources.
Conversation organization survives reconnect/restart through PostgreSQL. Sidebar expansion and width remain session preferences in memory; reload resets their default values. Search is literal and case-insensitive over titles and sent questions, including archives; accent-insensitive, semantic and answer-body search are intentionally absent. Shared retention/backup/authentication obligations remain unchanged. Manual acceptance should include dragging the desktop edge, using the collapsed shortcuts, renaming/pinning a prior conversation, archiving/restoring it, and cancelling deletion in the mobile drawer.

title: Corporate Agent Verification
heading: Intentional limits and next decisions
text:
Intentional limits and next decisions
Only sales is implemented. Conversation is bounded rather than an unrestricted general-knowledge assistant. Execution is process-local, not a durable workflow engine: crashed work is interrupted after the lease and never automatically resumed. Old temporary transcripts have no durable migration source. Stored answers are historical snapshots, not automatically refreshed ERP data.
Local development represents one local owner; production login/shared deployment remain PJ-05. Before shared use, PH-09 requires retention/provider/backup/identity decisions. PH-08 still requires a dedicated SELECT-only Oracle account, currency/weight confirmation and investigation of the legacy fetch discrepancy. PH-10 requires a committed immutable migration baseline before a supported durable release. These are not silently implemented by this review.
Manual interface acceptance should include toggling both themes, reopening an old conversation after closing the browser, continuing its filters, checking a clarification, reading the matched-products list and cancelling/confirming explicit deletion. The automated and real-browser checks do not replace the owner's assessment of conversational tone and presentation.

title: IA-MNS Human Actions
heading: Maintaining this checklist
text:
Maintaining this checklist
Inspect existing decisions, access, tools, configuration, and prior authorization before requesting human intervention. Complete authorized automation and all useful preparation first.
Keep one stable `PH-NN` ID per coherent action; never reuse or renumber IDs. Split broad items into independently verifiable actions as they become concrete, and add newly discovered actions immediately.
Every action retains its ID, checkbox, owner, status, dependency, and evidence. Active or conditional requests also need the exact action, reason, non-secret configuration names, and verification method. Use `pending`, `in progress`, `completed`, `blocked`, or `changed` consistently with the [plan](implementation-plan.md#maintaining-this-plan).
Before asking the user, provide a concrete request: the exact setting or decision, prepared options where appropriate, why automation cannot finish it, affected task IDs, and how completion will be checked.
If an action blocks work now, mark the dependent plan task `blocked`, link this entry, and surface the request to the user. Continue independent authorized work.
Use `[x]` and `completed` only after verification, recording safe evidence and the verification date. If direct verification is unavailable, record the limitation rather than claiming success.
Reopen an action with `[ ]` if later evidence invalidates completion, access expires, or configuration changes, and record why.
A conditional item that becomes unnecessary remains `[ ]` with status `changed`, an explicit reason, and its future trigger or replacement.

title: IA-MNS Human Actions
heading: Safe configuration handoff
text:
Safe configuration handoff
Record configuration names, required scopes, environment, purpose, non-secret resource identifiers, and secure destination. Never record passwords, tokens, API keys, connection strings containing credentials, private keys, or complete environment dumps here, in the plan, in chat, or in tracked example files.
Name only implemented configuration keys and link the [generated configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md); do not invent variable names in advance.
Humans place secrets directly into the selected protected secret store or an explicitly documented ignored local file. Contributors verify presence and authorized behavior without printing secret contents.
Use synthetic local and test data and ephemeral credentials where possible. Production secrets must not be prerequisites for ordinary development or CI.
